subject: Biology
title: What Makes a Plant a Plant?
description: Learn What Makes a Plant a Plant? in one minute.

hook.text: Plants don't eat, hunt, or move. Yet they conquered every continent, including Antarctica.

buildup.text: Plants are multicellular organisms that make their own food from sunlight, water, and CO₂.

discovery.text: They have cell walls made of cellulose and use chlorophyll to capture light energy.

twist.text: Plants evolved from green algae about 500 million years ago and transformed Earth's atmosphere.

climax.text: Without plants, there would be no oxygen, no food chains, and no life as we know it.

punchline.text: They can't move, but they rule the planet.

details.summary: Plants are multicellular eukaryotes that produce their own food through photosynthesis using chloroplasts, have cellulose cell walls, and typically live anchored in soil. They evolved from green algae over 470 million years ago and have since diversified into over 380,000 known species.
details.whyItMatters: Plants produce the oxygen we breathe, the food we eat, and the habitats most terrestrial life depends on. Understanding what defines a plant clarifies the boundary between kingdoms and reveals the adaptations enabling land colonization.
takeaways: Plants produce food through photosynthesis in chloroplasts containing chlorophyll
Cellulose cell walls provide structural support unique to the plant kingdom
Over 380,000 plant species have been described with more discovered each year

faq.question: What key adaptations allowed plants to move from water to land?
faq.answer: Waxy cuticle to prevent water loss, stomata to control gas exchange, vascular tissue for long-distance transport, roots for anchorage and absorption, and seeds that survive desiccation during dispersal. Each adaptation solved a specific challenge of life on land.

faq.question: Are all green organisms plants?
faq.answer: No. Green algae, cyanobacteria, and some protists photosynthesize but are not plants. Plants are specifically multicellular organisms descended from a green algal ancestor that colonized land. The distinction matters because these groups evolved photosynthesis independently or earlier.
